The Alligator Alcatraz Boondoggle
By Eric Schlosser June 4, 2026

Excellent reporting by Eric Schlosser in The Atlantic on how an immigration camp became one of the most expensive carceral facilities in U.S. history. Read the full piece:

www.theatlantic.com/ideas/2026/0...

By Schlosser's calculation, it would have cost less to buy each detained man a one-bedroom condo in Orlando and pay a full-time guard. Florida's emergency fund has dwindled to $200 million, not enough to keep the camp running through the year.

Eric Schlosser reports that perhaps three-quarters of the men held there have never been convicted of a crime. They are awaiting civil immigration hearings, not serving sentences. This is what it costs to run detention as political theater.

Florida built the camp through a no-bid emergency process that steered contracts to DeSantis donors. One firm with no detention experience got $78.5 million. It billed the state $959,088 for a single assistant camp manager. Florida's prisons director makes $203,434.

There is no plumbing, so a portable-toilet firm called Doodie Calls hauls about 45,000 gallons of waste a day. Florida paid it more than $92 million for six months and projects $480 million over two years. A sewage plant for a town of 10,000 costs about $5 million.
